chunks.chunk_text: IN THE HIGH COURT OF DELHI AT NEW DELHI W.P.(C) NO. 4812/2024 & CM APPL. 19842/2024 IN THE MATTER OF: Surender Sharma & Ors. ...Petitioners Versus Union of India & Anr. ...Respondents CORAM: HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE RAJESH CHATURVEDI ORDER DATED: 14.08.2024 1. The present writ petition has been filed under Article 226 challenging the demolition notice. 2. The petitioner claims title through registered Sale Deed dated 12.03.1998 for property bearing Plot No. 44, Khasra No. 312, Village Rangpuri, New Delhi. 3. Having heard learned counsel for both sides, this Court finds no merit in the petition. 4. The writ petition is accordingly DISMISSED with costs of Rs. 25,000/- to be deposited by the petitioner with the Delhi State Legal Services Authority within 30 days. 5. The statutory appeal period is limited to 45 days under Section 420 of the Municipal Act.

CENTRAL INFORMATION COMMISSION Baba Gangnath Marg, Munirka, New Delhi - 110067 DECISION FILE NO: CIC/MORTH/A/2025/001429 Appellant: Shri Arvind Mehta Public Authority: Ministry of Road Transport & Highways Date of Hearing: 22.01.2025 Date of Decision: 28.01.2025 FACTS OF THE CASE: 1. The Appellant sought details of toll collection concessionaire agreement for NH-48. 2. The CPIO wrongfully denied information under Section 8(1)(d) without substantiating commercial confidence. 3. Commission directs CPIO to provide complete agreement within 15 working days. 4. A show-cause notice is issued to CPIO under Section 20(1) imposing penalty of Rs. 15,000/- for malafide delay exceeding 60 days.
